title: XWayland-using window is not highlighted in Task Manager while showing child dialog window
line: An app's task now stays highlighted in the Task Manager while one of its dialogs is open, also for XWayland apps.
explanation: XWayland dialogs reach the task manager already active and already marked as transient of their main window, while the main window has just been reported inactive. The Wayland tasks model then made the main window the active task again in its internal state but never emitted a dataChanged for it, so the task manager kept drawing it as inactive until something else changed. The change emits IsActive changes for the old and new active task when a newly added window is active.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: notify views when a new transient activates its parent

A window that is already active when it appears, such as the modal
dialog of an XWayland app, made its parent the active task without
emitting a change, so the task stayed unhighlighted. Emit it now.

BUG: 512159

media.caption: Dolphin under XWayland, no dialog: its task is highlighted
Create New Folder open (dialog active): the task turns grey
With the fix, no dialog: task highlighted
With the fix, Create New Folder open: the task stays highlighted

review.text: Clean, minimal root-cause fix in WaylandTasksModel::Private::addWindow that emits IsActive dataChanged for both the previously active window and the newly effective active parent when a transient dialog arrives already active. WaylandTasksModel::Private::dataChanged safely ignores nullptr or not-yet-inserted windows via findWindow(), so regular new active windows and transient dialogs are both handled cleanly. The screenshots, regression checks, and commit description accurately match the patch.

reviews.text: Clean, minimal root-cause fix in WaylandTasksModel::Private::addWindow that emits IsActive dataChanged for both the previously active window and the newly effective active parent when a transient dialog arrives already active. WaylandTasksModel::Private::dataChanged safely ignores nullptr or not-yet-inserted windows via findWindow(), so regular new active windows and transient dialogs are both handled cleanly. The screenshots, regression checks, and commit description accurately match the patch.

Correct root cause in the right layer: in WaylandTasksModel::addWindow a window that arrives already active (an XWayland modal with its parent already set) silently set activeWindow to its parent without any dataChanged, so the view kept the parent unhighlighted. Emitting IsActive for both the previous and new active task fixes it and also covers the stale-highlight case when the old active window's deactivation arrives later; it runs before the new row is inserted, so the dataChanged for the new window itself is harmlessly skipped. Before/after shots clearly show the difference. The reporter's native LibreOffice variant was not reproducible, which the notes state honestly.
